steps.text: Wash clams to remove any dirt or sand.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic in hot oil until tender, about 1 minute.
Pour in white wine; bring to a boil. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Add clams, cover the pot, and steam just until clams start to open. Add butter, cover the pot, and continue cooking until most or all of the clams open. Discard any clams that do not open.
Transfer clams and broth to 2 large bowls. Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Scott Ure's Clams and Garlic
raw_recipe.description: This garlic butter clams recipe steams little neck clams in a buttery, garlicky white wine broth that's perfect served over pasta with crusty bread.
raw_recipe.name: Scott Ure's Clams and Garlic

review.reviewBody:
My only "complaint" about this recipe is that I wish it stated at what temperature to "steam" the clams. My husband and I had quite a disagreement. He wanted to bring it to a boil and then almost shut the heat off. I thought it would be hot enough. Our compromise was to turn the heat to medium for about 20 minutes. 49 out of the 50 clams opened. I was shocked to see how much liquor they make. I thought the small amount of wine wouldn't be enough.
They were great. Definitely have a lot of crusty bread on hand. Linguine or some other pasta is great. My kids were so brave about trying them. I can't wait to make it again. We added some fresh lemon after they were cooked and it really brought out the flavor. Delicious!
Oh, and scrub the clams really well. I got a lot of sand and gunk off them.
THANKS for a great recipe.

I make this recipe all the time. I add 1/2 tsp of red pepper flakes to infuse the garlic while it is simmering. When clams are done I strain the broth through a tight strainer or cheesecloth to keep out any sand grit. Lastly, I add a touch of tomato paste for color and depth in the sauce, add 1 tablespoon of butter and swirl and fresh chopped parsley - - and then when I pour the clams into a bowl, I wet a dish towel, put it in the microwave for 1 minute, pour the sauce over the clams and cover with the hot wet towel to keep the clams hot and steamy until everyone is ready to eat! 
Mangia!

Used 150 little neck clams! A stick of butter, good white wine, and I used McCormick's California Style Garlic Powder that had parsley in it....also added a lil chili powder. Added 2 lbs of shrimp and some andouille sausage. Put everything in a big disposable tin pan covered with foil and let steam on the grill until the shrimp were done and clam opened....delicious! Used the broth in the bottom of the pan for dipping crusty bread. Just amazing!

This was really excellent! I am so glad I made it. I am a veteran clam cooker, so I'll share my observations/changes. I used 50 little neck clams. I used about 9 cloves of garlic. I saw other reviewers used red pepper flakes, so I added 1/2 fresh minced jalapeno pepper which I sauteed with the garlic. 

I added 2 cups seafood broth from a carton and brought the heat to high for about 2 minutes to reduce to about 1/3.

Reduced heat to medium and added the clams. I usually steam clams with some liquid at fairly high heat. Keeping these at medium heat increased the cooking time (duh). I covered the pot and waited from them to start opening - about 10 minutes. Added the butter (4 tbsp), stirred and covered for probably another 8 minutes. 

Then added 1/2 cup chopped parsley, 1/4 snipped fresh chives, and the juice of 1/2 lemon.

Excellent! Served with a loaf of crusty french bread toasted in the oven for a bit. Loved it. DH loved it.

This served 2 with leftovers; could have served 3 reasonable people.

This is a great recipe, thanks Scott!

I bought middlenecks by mistake so came searching for a good recipe that might make them as tender as possible. Score! I followed exactly but made sure to use UNSALTED butter since I knew the clams were salty enough on their own. Also, the picture shows lemon, but nothing in the recipe about it. I highly recommend a few squeezes of fresh lemon right at serving time. Also, for novices, try to remove the clams as soon as they open - don't wait for all of them to finish or the early ones may toughen up.

This is the first time making steamed clams. I followed the recipe exactly. I thought 1/2 cup of parsley was too much. Next time I will reduce it to 1/4 cup. I will also soak the clams instead of just rinsing them to remove more of the salt. The broth was very good. I used Pinot Grigio wine and added 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes. I steamed the clams for 6 minutes on high. The broth was great for dunking the crusty Italian bread.

This was fantastic! My daughter has a dairy allergy so I just left out the butter and added a bit of EVOO at the end and every bit was eaten! For those who were wondering about cook time I did 12 clams (serving for 1) and covered at med heat for 5 mins and everything opened up beautifully. I also took the clams out and reduced the sauce and tossed with spaghetti for a perfect meal for 1.

Delicious, easy and quick! I'm definitely going to make this again! the only differences was adding 1 onion with the garlic as well as a hand full of cherry tomatoes (sliced in half) once I add the wine. It adds a bit of sweetness while the wine reduces.

Wow, these are restaurant quality as they are! They really allow the clam flavor to be the star. Yum.
However, what made them even better were a few changes... I sauteed a 1/2 cup of chopped yellow onions with the garlic and it gave the tad of sweetness it needed. I also added 1/2 cup of clam juice after reducing the wine, 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (or more for an extra kick) and garnished it with the chopped parsley AND the zest of one lemon. My family ate it with freshly baked french bread and it was heavenly. Thanks for this recipe!

I live in Ha Noi, Viet Nam, and I say these clams, for only 17,000VND kg. ($0.80US) was a great deal! So, I looked for a quick and easy recipe and I found this one. One problem here is that a bottle of wine is very expensive with import fees and more. So, I looked for a replacement for wine. I learned that grape juice (red or white) can be used and that adding a teaspoon of vinegar to it would give it that "wine" flavor. I did just that and followed the rest of the recipe. Everything worked well and, yes, I kept the liquid at a low boil and could see that the steam was just going everywhere. The flavor was more than wonderful! The smell of the food was more than enticing. It "looked" very good as well. So, my Vietnamese friend, who told me that does not like clams at all, tried them and she just loved them! THAT is a real tribute to the recipe!

I strongly recommend this recipe and, as was stated in other reviews, the liquid from the clams keeps enough of the liquids going and ALL of the clams opened! So, bon appetit!

I make this recipe often. It's simple but delicious. A couple of things I do differently........after scrubbing clams I leave them covered in salted water for a few hours and add cornmeal. This will help purge any sand inside the clams. As others have mentioned I also add red pepper flakes and instead of adding butter while they cook, I make a roux and thicken the broth after removing the open clams. I prefer a thicker texture when dunking my crusty Italian bread !!!
I have been using this recipe and serving it over linguine or spaghetti - everyone I ever served it to just loves it. It is my go to recipe when I want to make linguine and clam sauce.

Made it as written and loved it. As a coastal New Englander, I can't think of a way to improve it other than calling out that you should always purge your clams before steaming, which is just letting them sit in cold salt water with a little corn starch for an hour or so to get them to spit out any sand. I like to serve steamed clams with small bowls of broth and melted butter for dipping, along with crusty bread.
Been making these for years, everyone loves them.

My husband and I love steamed little necks. We always just steamed them and then dipped them in butter. WOW what a difference this recipe has made for us! I actually do ours in my wok for some reason, and have made it so many times successfully you can't go wrong with this as your base or if you doctor it up. We usually use less clams and eat as an appetizer with toasted croutons that I make from another recipe on this site. One last comment, Scott includes the step to clean the clams, and he is spot on. I scrub them with a brush under cold water and then put them in a bowl with refrigerated water and let them soak while I make the croutons and other dishes. Works very well, and we rarely if ever get any sand anymore. Thank you Scott Ure!!!
Made this years ago and would still say this is THE best recipe.
Have prepared this a few times, typically with only two dozen Clams, I simply halve the Recipe. Very enjoyable over Linguine.
This recipe is quick, I finished with lemon. Served with crusty bread and pasta. I will keep this as a go to. Delicious 🤤
